key_insight: Across tested LLMs, stronger self-evaluation expressiveness coincided with weaker confidence calibration.
engineering_relevance: Systems that rely on LLM self-assessment should evaluate both correctness discrimination and confidence calibration before trusting model-reported certainty.
method: Extend classical VC theory with Probabilistic VC (PVC) to measure confident classification capacity.
Add Calibration-aware PVC (C-PVC) to require alignment between confidence and actual success rates.
Have models choose between two self-generated solutions and report confidence.
evidence_signal: Tests of eleven 7–8B models on 360 original math problems, TruthfulQA, and CommonsenseQA found s1.1-7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct highest in PVC-VUS, while JiuZhang3.0-7B had the lowest ECE.
watch_item: Ground truth came from an ensemble of larger models, so evaluator errors could affect the measured trade-off.
paper_title: Can LLMs Reliably Evaluate Themselves? A Probabilistic VC Framework
